---
title: "Why"
subtitle: "Readers keep failing on the same few facts"
---

Readers of array data (browsers, catalogs, analysis tools, agents) keep
failing on a small set of facts that a store's metadata holds, or fails to
hold:

- the grid is given as coordinate arrays, so a reader must test regularity
  from data instead of reading it from a declaration;
- 2-D longitude and latitude arrays hide a grid that is regular in some
  projected CRS ("cryptic curvilinear"), which four numbers and a CRS string
  describe exactly;
- 1-D nominal axes look regular and are wrong (ocean model tripolar grids);
- CF packing, fill values and units decide the colour of every pixel and are
  read inconsistently;
- chunking set for the source files (one row, or 25 depth levels, per chunk)
  is carried into virtual stores, where it sets the read cost of every view;
- referenced bytes live on hosts with their own CORS behaviour.

Each of these is checkable from metadata. A card records them once, so a
person, an agent or a viewer can decide before fetching data.

## What the fixtures have shown

The project grew out of building browser fixtures for the Portolan Zarr
profile (portolan-sdi/portolan-spec issue 132). The hard cases turned out to
be interpretation problems, not rendering problems: a viewer cannot fix them,
a declaration can.

**Transport works.** Pawsey Acacia and source.coop both serve cross-origin
range reads. A browser drew a fixture straight from the bucket.

**Packing is ignored.** The reference renderer drew CF-packed int16 OISST as
raw integers against a ramp in physical units: the whole ocean saturated.

![f01b in the reference renderer: geometry right, ocean saturated because
`scale_factor` was not applied](img/f01b-first-draw.png)

**Fill values are not treated as missing** unless STAC `nodata` says so;
land drew as the bottom colour. Writers disagree too: xarray's default for
Zarr v3 writes `fill_value` 0 beside a CF `_FillValue` of -999, and -1e20
stored as float32 never equals the float64 attribute, so masking silently
fails.

**Source hosts decide whether virtual stores can draw.** NCEI sends
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; the NSIDC data host sends none, so the
G02202 virtual store cannot be read from any browser, wherever its index is
hosted.

**Virtual stores inherit source chunking.** Bremen ASI is one row per chunk;
ACCESS-ESM1.6 packs 25 depth levels per chunk. Both exceed the draft
profile's amplification bound of 8.

**Indexes drop interpretation.** The G02202 virtual store has no grid
mapping; the ACCESS-ESM1.6 store names `geolon_t geolat_t` in `coordinates`
but does not carry them, leaving 1-D nominal axes that are wrong north of the
tripolar fold.

**The heuristics find the known cases unprompted** across the rasterwise
problem-file archive: Mercator-spaced latitude, swapped axes, and five files
with only 2-D lon/lat that are candidates for a grid fit.

Details: [first results](https://github.com/hypertidy/storecard/blob/main/portolan/docs/results-2026-11-06.md)
and the [fixtures plan](https://github.com/hypertidy/storecard/blob/main/portolan/docs/fixtures-plan.md).
